To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interruption of blood supply without invading bone integrity results in a marked increase of bone turnover, which is compensated by an equivalent amount of bone formation.
devascularization of rat tibiae resulted in a marked stimulation of bone turnover (resorbing and forming surfaces) during the first two months.
bone resorption and bone formation increase in parallel in devascularized bone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of vascular interruption on bone.
the effects of bone devasculatization on bone metabolism.
the effects of bone devascularity on bone resorption and the resultant changes in bone mass.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bone response to interruption of its blood supply was to increase its turnover without altering the mass of bone.
the interruption of blood supply in bone results in increased bone turnover without affecting the resultant bone mass.
the bone devascularization in rats resulted in a transient increase in bone resorptive and formative activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bone devascularization in isotope-prelabeled rats caused an increased turnover of the skeleton, without any change in the resultant mass of calcium and collagen.
the interruption of blood supply without invading bone integrity does not cause bone loss.
bone devascularization stimulates bone resorption and bone formation in a way that the resultant bone mass remains constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bone devascularization results in a marked increase of bone turnover, but does not affect bone mass.
the interruption of blood supply does not necessarily cause osteoporosis, and the effects of bone devascualrization are reversible.
